summary: Adds new access identifiers to the IMAP URL scheme, which can restrict who may use URLs created with URLAUTH. The existing identifiers in RFC 5092 could not handle new services like streaming, and this extends them for that purpose.

eli5.summary: An IMAP URL is like a ticket to a mail item. This adds new kinds of ticket stamps so tickets can say who may use them, even for streaming.

questions: what is an imap urlauth access identifier
what is the imap stream access identifier
what is submit+ in imap url
how do i register a new imap url access identifier
subtitle: New access identifiers for URLAUTH IMAP URLs, so services such as streaming can fetch mail on a user's behalf without abusing submit+.

tldr.problem: IMAP URLs made with URLAUTH can limit who may use them, but the only identifier for entities acting on a user's behalf was submit+, which is unsuitable as a general mechanism.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC allows any application name to be an access identifier or, with a plus and a userid, an access identifier prefix, creates an IANA registry for them, and registers a new stream identifier.
tldr.outcome: New services can get their own, separately administered access identifiers. The RFC updates RFC 5092 and is the master for the IANA entries of the existing identifiers.

today: RFC 5593 is a Proposed Standard published in June 2009 and updates RFC 5092. The unit metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why More Access Identifiers
sections.content:
The IMAP URL specification (RFC 5092) lets URLs carry authorization information through URLAUTH. An <access> identifier in the URL limits who may use it, for example only anonymous users, authenticated users or message submission entities.

RFC 5593 points out that there was no way to create new identifiers, and that overloading the existing ones has security and administrative implications. It adds a new identifier, stream, for message streaming entities, and an IANA registration template for future ones.

It updates RFC 5092 and should be taken as the master if the two differ on the IANA definitions of the existing identifiers.
sections.eli5: A ticket to a mail item can already say who may use it. This adds a way to invent new kinds of ticket for new jobs.

sections.title: The Existing Identifiers
sections.content:
RFC 5092 defines two identifiers. authuser limits a URL to authenticated IMAP sessions logged in as any non-anonymous user. anonymous means use is not restricted by the session's authorization identity.

It also defines two prefixes that are followed by a userid. submit+ means only a userid authorized as a message submission entity on behalf of that user may use the URL. user+ limits use to IMAP sessions logged in as the specified userid.
sections.eli5: There were four kinds of ticket: anyone, any logged-in person, one named person, or the post office working for a named person.

sections.title: Why submit+ Is Not Enough
sections.content:
The existing identifiers suit user-based authorization, but only submit+ covers entities acting for a user. New services such as streaming need generic support for such external entities, and the RFC gives three reasons not to stretch submit+ for that.

  • Security: the IMAP server keeps a list of submission servers allowed to fetch submit+ URLs. Adding every possible external entity to that list would increase the attack surface.
  • Administration: when such an entity presents a URLAUTH URL, the server logs do not show what it was for.
  • Resourcing: without a way to tell applications apart, the server cannot prioritize resources for particular ones.
sections.eli5: If every helper had to use the post office's ticket, the post office's guest list would get long and risky, and nobody could tell what each helper was doing.

sections.title: How New Identifiers Work
sections.content:
An additional identifier MUST take one of two forms. It is either an access identifier, which is the application name such as exampleapp, or an access identifier prefix, which is the name followed by + and a userid, such as exampleapp3+testuser. A name can be registered in both forms, but that needs two separate IANA registrations.

The semantics match submit+: only a userid authorized as an application entity for that application may use the URL. For prefixes, the IMAP server SHALL NOT validate the userid in the URL, but MUST validate that the IMAP session's authorization identity is authorized as an application entity for that application. The application entity itself MAY validate the userid before fetching.

The server therefore needs an extensible way to register applications and associate userids with them. If an application foo is created, URLs with the identifier foo are checked against the list of userids associated with foo.
sections.eli5: Each helper job gets its own named guest list. A ticket stamped with that job's name only works for people on that job's list.

sections.title: Formal Syntax and the stream Identifier
sections.content:
The ABNF extends the access rule from RFC 5092 with an application made of one or more letters or digits, either on its own or followed by + and an encoded user. Strings are case-insensitive, and implementations MUST accept them that way.

The first application is streaming of multimedia files received as messaging attachments. The stream identifier is registered for it, and it is described as used by SIP Media Servers to retrieve attachments for streaming to email clients.
sections.eli5: The rule is simple: a job name, optionally followed by a plus and a person's name. The first new job name is stream.

sections.title: The IANA Registry
sections.content:
IANA created a registry for IMAP URLAUTH access identifiers and prefixes. New entries MUST be registered under the IETF Review policy. A registration gives the type (identifier or prefix), the application name, a description, the RFC number and a contact.

The RFC also supplies the entries for the existing identifiers and prefixes from RFC 5092 and for stream.
sections.eli5: There is now an official book where each new ticket kind is written down, with what it is for and who to ask about it.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The extension generalizes the submit+ idea to arbitrary applications. Its main purpose is security: to avoid overloading submit+ as a generic way for entities to fetch IMAP URLs on behalf of userids. Otherwise the security implications are the same as those in Section 10.1 of RFC 5092.
sections.eli5: Giving each job its own list is safer than putting every helper on one big list.
